newsitem.title: CHINA: China yuan business to begin this week - official.
newsitem.headline: China yuan business to begin this week - official.

text.p: Two foreign banks will begin conducting local Chinese currency business on either Thursday or Friday, the head of the People's Bank of China Shanghai branch, Mao Yingliang, said on Wednesday.
Mao told a seminar that preparations for the start of Chinese yuan business by foreign banks had been completed.
He declined to name the two banks.
Asked about the tax rate the foreign banks will be charged for local currency business, Mao said this was the responsibility of the central tax authorities.
Previous statements have indicated foreign banks will be charged at a rate of 15 percent, the same as for foreign exchange business.

Eight foreign banks have so far been approved to handle local currency business in Shanghai on the precondition that they move their branches to the city's premier economic development zone of Pudong.
So far, four banks have done so, including Citibank of the United States, and the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp.
